in.other_title: Irving et al.: stock amplification (Christiano et al.) needs humans to generate strong subquestions
in.rationale: Christiano et al. (2018) build training targets from a human (or learned human model) decomposing questions for copies of the agent; the authors argue this needs a human questioner able to produce strong consistency checks, a limitation debate avoids. It is a conceptual argument with no new data, and the authors present the two schemes as approximately equivalent once amplification adds an adversarial Questioner, so CRITIQUES of a specific assumption rather than CHALLENGES.
in.scope: proposed CRITIQUES: Whether amplification's human-generated decomposition limits it relative to debate; holds for stock amplification with a supervised Questioner, not for variants with an adversarial Questioner

text: The authors state that the key assumption underlying Iterated Amplification is that a human can coordinate multiple copies of X to perform better than a single copy of X. They discuss this assumption in the context of whether amplification can be applied to complex real-world tasks beyond human scale.
title: Key assumption: a human can coordinate copies of X to beat a single copy
